description.narrative: Impact /Overall Objective: Regional trade liberalization and integration contributes to increased sustainable economic development and reduced poverty in PAFTA countries Outcome 1: PAFTA Sec. coordinates the PAFTA competently Output 1.1 PAFTA sec. staff have acquired modern knowledge on customs union affairs from international/regional experts Output 1.2 PAFTA sec. staff have acquired new skills in mediation & management from attending local trainings Outcome 2: Negotiators &Focal points in LDC’s engage on PAFTA with PAFTA Sec. in ways that benefits their country Output 2.1 LAS trade training program is developed tailored to the needs of LDC’s FPs and Negotiators Output 2.2 All LDC’s FP and Negotiators, have acquired new skills from LAS trade training programs Output 2.3 All PAFTA members engage and network in joint trade negotiation workshops
Stöd till LAS i analys inför omförhandling av PAFTA
Support to LAS analyzis re-negotiating PAFTA

The project was limited in terms of both scope and scale. It was also the first direct agreement between Sida and the League of Arab States whereas the other partnerships have been through intermediaries such as UNIDO. The results are therefore limited, but they include: 1. LAS staff aquired capacity on various trade topics and were able to support member states in the finalization of the trade in services negotiations under the Pan-Arab Free trade area. 2. The Economic departement of LAS are now more structured and organized to handle the day to day work of suppport to member states on various trade topics which has improved the overall satisfaction from member states. 3. The PAFTA-secretariat has improved there skills in organizing trainings and seminars on various topics and in various countries with increased satisfaction from members. Also increased number of participating women. 4. The support has also managed to support LAS in movement on the establishment of a dispute settlement mechanism for the implementation of the PAFTA. Since the project has not been evaluated, it is difficult to thoroughly assess the overall results. LAS has limited capacity, and there has been various political challenges during the project implemention. It seens however that LAS has been able to strengthen certain aspects of its institutional capacity.
